_doc: Agent role -> model chain, tried in order through Meterless Nightshift only. Edit this file, not the code. Every model is NVIDIA. The safety critic, dry run, restraint gate and executor are deterministic code and have no model. `app` is the meterless-app name sent with a role's calls and model_apps the app pinned to each model: Nightshift routes by the app's rule, so each app name has a one-lane allowlist in Nightshift (state/app-policy.json): shopfloor-os -> Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, shopfloor-os-fast -> Nemotron 3.5 Lightning. data/model_probe.json (scripts/probe_models.py) records which models Nightshift actually serves.

router.why: Orchestrator hops: a small decision over a short state, many times per incident: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B A3B (3B active) for the lowest latency.

monitor.why: A one-line summary for the supervisor; the classification itself is rules.

planner.why: Grounded multi-constraint planning with clause citations: the deep reasoning model.

coordinator.why: Splits an open question into sub-tasks over the table catalogue: deep reasoning.

sql_agent.why: Writes Spark SQL: Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, the strongest model this Nightshift serves. Llama-3.3-Nemotron-Super 49B can only be a Nightshift verify lane, NVIDIA's endpoint for Nemotron 3 Super 120B is not enabled for this key (404), and the coder models in the list are non-NVIDIA local models that would load on the PC.

analyst.why: Correlates evidence into cited findings: deep reasoning.

evidence_critic.why: Checks the analyst's claims against the rows: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a different model from the analyst (Super VL), for an independent check. It can only drop claims, after the rule-based number check.

lab.why: Proposes one testable policy change from history: deep reasoning.

sentinel.why: Triage of ambiguous floor signals only (the rules decide the clear ones): a quick yes/no with a reason, so the fast model.
